_doc: ⚑ S227 — LAMBYOS HOME, first pass (docs/reinterp/LAMBYOS_HOME_DESIGN_2026-10-09.md; W1-A1/A2/A4/A5/A7). The programme's front door, the way Bob was Windows': a flat illustrated 1997 living room (src/desktop/home/), one object = one thing to learn, each opening a plain card in the FRAME's voice. It replaces the orienting card (src/desktop/orientingCard.ts) as the first thing a fresh reinterp load shows; that card survives as the SHORT DOOR (`?home=0`, and the notice's 'Been here before?' line). THE FRAME'S WORDS ARE NOT COPIED HERE: the content note, premise, about, subtitle, version tag, the three ways to look (`cards.*`), the menu line, captions, Leave's left page and the wait/enter notes are read from data/strings/orientingCard.json, unchanged, so the two doors can never drift apart (design §1: 'the words already in orientingCard.json … reused verbatim'). This file holds only what is new to Home. HIS ANSWERS (design §7, 2026-10-09/10): (1) 'only speech bubbles like BOB' — Lamby is in the room and speaks ONLY in bubbles (`lamby.*`), the programme's own voice (register operable), short, never over the content note (every bubble is hidden while any card is open), always dismissible; no bubble ever carries a frame word. (2) 'Record? no' — Home files nothing: no ledger record, no witness entry; only the two view settings carry over in memory (the look mode and `ledger.view.captions`). (3) The Lexicon is NOT in Home at the start: it appears when the Close returns to Home (later). (4)/(6) The advert on the tape is his choice (c) and 'both', but it needs its drawing: in this pass the tape sits on the sideboard, drawn and named, and cannot be pressed. THE ONE GATE (design §1): the notice ('Before you come in') is the only thing lit at the start; closing it starts the existing 4 s arm-delay, after which the three enter buttons light. THE CUT (his 2026-10-10 ruling 'both': the exhibition offers the full piece AND the Speedrun Version, W1-A3): one quiet choice in each device card, default the full piece, `?cut=speedrun` preselects; src/state/cut.ts, memory only. `door.note` is new frame wording (this Leave is today's door's Leave, 'You left. / Nothing was kept.', not the menu's leave page, so gameMenu.leaveNote would have said the wrong thing). `armchair.body` is `chooseNote` without its first sentence ('Choose one.' belongs to the devices). `mat` is the programme's signage, drawn in the room's pixel type.

objects.notice: The notice: before you come in
objects.tablet: The tablet: on a phone or tablet

notice.title: Before you come in
notice.shortDoor: Been here before? Take the short door.

armchair.title: The turn
armchair.body: You never walk, and nothing is timed — turning to look is the only thing your body has to do.

door.title: Leave
door.note: Leaving now ends it here, before anything has started. Nothing is kept. Inside the piece, Leave is always in the menu.

lamby._doc: The programme's voice (LambyOS, register operable): cosy, a little too eager, and it never explains anything the frame explains. No line mentions the notice, the content, leaving, or what the piece is about.
lamby.greet: Welcome home! Everything is set up already.
lamby.greetAgain: Welcome home again! Everything is set up already.
chatter: I'm Lamby. I look after the house.
Make yourself comfortable. We chose everything in here for you.
When you're ready, the machines are on the little table.
You don't need to do anything.
lamby.armchair: Our best chair. It turns right round!
